chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying:

A man peeped at the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله through the palm-stalk screen, so the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said to him: If I knew that you would remain there, I would have come to you with a broad arrowhead until I gouged out your eye.
He said: So I said, Is that for us as well? He said: Woe to you—or alas for you—I tell you that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did it, and you say: Is that for us as well?

key_terms.أَفْقَأَ: to gouge out or burst an eye
key_terms.اطَّلَعَ: looked in or peeped into a private space
key_terms.النَّبِيِّ: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, whose conduct is being cited as authoritative
key_terms.الْجَرِيدِ: the palm-stalk screen or partition through which the man looked
key_terms.الْمِشْقَصِ: a broad arrowhead or sharp pointed instrument
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, whose action is presented as proof
key_terms.وَيْحَكَ: an expression of rebuke and warning

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about peeping into another person’s private space without permission?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that a man looked in upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله without permission, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله strongly condemned the act. The Imam عليه السلام then rebukes the questioner for hesitating about whether the Prophet’s ruling and practice apply, underscoring the authority of the Prophetic sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding violations of privacy.
